brief.todays_call: Brent last printed $94.11 — oil feed dark today as global markets thin into Eid-ul-Azha. The $17 retreat from the May $111 peak holds; import-bill arithmetic favourable at ~$680M/month of relief. The live structural story: IMF's new 3-year reform programme arrives while government bank borrowing has crossed its annual target in nine months. External shock premium unwinding — but the fiscal absorber that should capture the gain is itself overstretched. Book stays defensive on demand certainty through H2.

sections.tldr: NPL and CAR held on Q4 print; IMF reshapes recapitalization clock.
sections.analysis: NPL at 35.73% and CAR at 1.56% — both Q4 2025 prints, pending Q1 disclosure. The new IMF 3-year reform programme shifts the structural calculus: conditionality will include recapitalization targets and NPL resolution timelines that State-Owned Commercial Banks (SCBs) have deferred since the crisis. Government bank borrowing crossing its annual target in nine months sharpens the circularity — the sovereign balance sheet that must fund bank rescues is itself drawing banking-system liquidity beyond plan. The BSEC governance code overhaul addresses listed-firm transparency but does not touch the capital adequacy gap driving sector risk. Zero duration on bank paper until Q1 data prints and IMF conditionality terms arrive.

sections.tldr: Borrowing exceeds target in 9 months; budget June 7 the next catalyst.
sections.analysis: Government bank borrowing at BDT 0.92tn has crossed the annual target in nine months — fiscal financing running well ahead of plan. The IMF agreement on a 3-year reform programme provides an external financing lifeline but introduces conditionality constraining FY27 budget parameters on both revenue and expenditure. ADB's $5B five-year programme commitment adds project-level depth but does not address the recurrent fiscal gap. The binding constraint: fiscal consolidation conditionality arrives while private credit growth sits at 6.03% and NPL at 35.73% — the sovereign that must fund bank recapitalization is itself borrowing beyond plan. Budget June 7 is the decision point.

sections.title: Iran War & Oil
sections.verdict: Brent last at $94.11 — feed dark pre-Eid; $17 off May peak, import-bill relief persists.
sections.tldr: Brent feed dark; last print $94.11, $17 below May peak.
sections.analysis: Brent feed dark this session — last print $94.11, flat from the prior session's $6 crash through $100. The $17 decline from the May $111 peak represents cumulative import-bill relief of ~$680M/month, partially offsetting reserves pressure from ACU settlements and narrowing the trade gap. The question from the prior session stands: is $90–95 a floor or a pause before further demand-driven decline. WTI last at $90.55, Brent-WTI spread compressed to $3.56 as the geopolitical premium continues unwinding. For BD-exposed energy credit, the demand-destruction signal matters more than the level — crude declining at this velocity typically leads global demand by 2–3 months, putting garment order books in the crosshairs. Treasury desks: bank the import-bill gain and model $85–95 for H2.
